POST / creates an incident under an attacker-supplied jobId; the existence check (line 331) never binds the job to the caller's customer/worker scope, so a customer can file incidents against another customer's job.

PUT /:id has checks only for field_worker (reportedById) and dispatcher (region); a customer can update any incident by id, including status, assignedToId, internalNotes, and resolution of other tenants' incidents.
POST /:id/resolve is dispatcher/ops_admin only but has no region check, so a dispatcher can resolve incidents belonging to other regions by id.

`deserialize` deserializes input with an API that reconstructs behaviour (functions, prototypes, or arbitrary object graphs), not just data. Whoever controls the serialized bytes controls what is rebuilt in this process. Use a data-only format such as JSON with an explicit schema check.

POST /:id/assign omits the dispatcher region check that PUT/:id and DELETE/:id perform, so a dispatcher can reassign/act on jobs in any region by id.

POST /:id/status only gates field_worker against assignedWorkerId; customer and dispatcher roles pass through, so any authenticated user can mutate the status (incl. complete/cancel) of any job selected by the attacker-controlled :id.
POST /:id/reschedule updates any job by attacker-controlled :id with no dispatcher-region binding, enabling cross-region job rescheduling.
DELETE /:id cancels any job by attacker-controlled :id without the dispatcher-region check used elsewhere, enabling cross-region job cancellation.
